newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians forecast trouble if Jews settle in.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians forecast trouble if Jews settle in.

text.p: Palestinian residents forecast nothing but trouble if the Israeli municipality goes ahead with plans for a Jewish settler enclave in their Arab East Jerusalem neighbourhood.

The city granted a permit on Thursday to Irving Moskowitz, a U.S. Jewish businessman who bankrolls Jewish settlement in occupied areas, to build for Jews in the midst of Ras al-Amoud, a hilltop neighbourhood of 11,000.
"If they are asking for confrontation they will get it," said Taher, 18, who just graduated from high school.
The hilltop neighbourhood overlooks the golden Dome of the Rock in the walled Old City of Jerusalem.

"I fear that the foundation of these Jewish houses will again be built at the expense of lives of Palestinian youth, like what happened in Jabal Abu Ghneim," 37-year-old taxi driver, Ahmad Ali, told Reuters.

Israeli-PLO peace talks ground to a halt and clashes erupted when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground in March for the Jewish settlement of Har Homa on Jabal Abu Ghneim, another hilltop in East Jerusalem.

Israel's Jerusalem City Council took the decision to build a Jewish enclave in Ras al-Amoud late on Thursday, and Netanyahu rushed out a statement vowing to prevent the plan from going ahead at a time of crisis in peacemaking.

Palestinians charge Israel has stolen their land in East Jerusalem, an area occupied by the Jewish state in the 1967 war and claimed as part of Israel's undivided capital -- a claim not recognised by the international community.
Some Palestinians have accused Israel of trying to squeeze them out of East Jerusalem, which they want as the capital of a future state.

"My brothers moved out of Jerusalem because the Israeli municipality won't give them permits to build or add levels to our house, and here they are allowing to build more for Jews," Taher told Reuters.
Ali disputed Israeli Mayor Ehud Olmert's assertion he was building also for Palestinians in East Jerusalem.
"It seems when Olmert said he has plans to improve Arab Jerusalem, he meant he is improving it so that Jews will come and live there."

Resident Dawoud Abbasi told Reuters: "They don't have the right to build here, but they have the power to do whatever they like. We have nobody to back us...They have America...This is not democracy".
